title: Adversarial Example Explorer
description: Interactive p5.js MicroSim that lets students add an imperceptible Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) perturbation to a hand-drawn digit and watch a classifier's confidence flip from the correct class to an attacker-chosen target class.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Explain why a model's decision boundary admits adversarial examples by manipulating an input and watching classifier confidence change.
Relate the perturbation's L-infinity norm to its human visibility and its effect on the classifier.
prerequisites: Basic idea of a classifier and confidence scores

instructionalStrategies: Have students predict the magnitude at which the prediction flips, then test.
Use 'Show perturbation only' to discuss imperceptibility versus model sensitivity.

assessmentQuestions.question: Why does the digit still look like a 3 to you while the classifier reads it as an 8?
What does the L-infinity norm bound guarantee about the attack?
